subject: fluid_mechanics
title: Characteristics Studies of a Centrifugal Pump
aim: To study the performance characteristics of a centrifugal pump at constant speed and determine its operating heads, discharge, input power, output power, and overall efficiency.
apparatus: Centrifugal pump coupled with 1.0 HP AC motor (1420 rpm)
Sump tank and collecting tank (0.35 m × 0.35 m)
Vacuum gauge on suction side (mm Hg)
theory:
A centrifugal pump is a rotodynamic machine that converts mechanical energy into hydraulic energy. As the impeller rotates, fluid enters axially through the eye of the impeller and is thrown radially outward by centrifugal force into the spiral casing (volute). Kinetic energy is converted into pressure energy before discharging.

Suction Head:
H_s = \frac{P_s \times 133.3}{\rho g} = P_s \times 0.0136 \quad (\text{m of water})

Delivery Head:
H_d = \frac{P_d \times 9.81 \times 10^4}{\rho g} = P_d \times 10 \quad (\text{m of water})

Total Operating Head:
H_T = H_d + H_s + Z \quad (\text{m of water}) \quad \text{where } Z = 0.85\text{ m}

Actual Discharge Rate:
Q_{act} = \frac{A_{tank} \times rise}{t} = \frac{0.35 \times 0.35 \times 0.1}{t} = \frac{0.01225}{t} \quad (\text{m}^3/\text{s})

Electrical Input Power:
I_p = \frac{N \times 3600 \times 1000}{T \times 1200} = \frac{30000}{T} \quad (\text{Watts})

Pump Hydraulic Output Power:
O_p = \rho \cdot g \cdot H_T \cdot Q_{act} = 1000 \times 9.81 \times H_T \times Q_{act} \quad (\text{Watts})

Overall Efficiency:
\eta = \frac{O_p}{I_p} \times 100 \quad (\%)
procedure: Ensure the sump tank has sufficient clean water and check for proper pump priming.
Fully open the suction valve and ensure the delivery valve is closed.
Switch on the electric motor to run the centrifugal pump at constant rated speed (1420 rpm).
Gradually open the discharge delivery valve to set the desired delivery pressure.
Record the suction vacuum gauge reading (Ps in mm Hg) and delivery pressure gauge reading (Pd in kg/cm²).
Measure the time taken (t in sec) for a 10 cm (0.1 m) water level rise in the collecting tank.
Note the time taken (T in sec) for 10 revolutions of the energy meter disc.
Repeat the observations for 5 different discharge flow rates across the operating range.
Compute Hs, Hd, HT, Qact, Ip, Op, and overall efficiency η for each trial.

calculations.label: Step 3: Total Operating Head (HT)
calculations.formula_latex: H_T = H_d + H_s + Z = H_d + H_s + 0.85

calculations.label: Step 6: Pump Output Water Power (Op)

formulas.label: Suction Head (Hs)
formulas.derivation:
Conversion of suction vacuum gauge reading in mm Hg to equivalent meters of water column:

H_s = \frac{P_s \times 133.322}{1000 \times 9.81} = P_s \times 0.01359 \approx P_s \times 0.0136 \text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates suction vacuum lift in meters of water.
assumptions: Standard atmospheric and liquid mercury conversion constants
formulas.practical_application: Assesses suction line lift capacity and NPSH limits.

formulas.label: Delivery Head (Hd)
formulas.purpose: Calculates delivery discharge head in meters of water.
formulas.practical_application: Measures effective delivery pressure head developed across discharge line.

formulas.label: Total Head (HT)
formulas.derivation:
Sum of delivery head, suction head, and the vertical distance between the two pressure gauges:

H_T = H_d + H_s + 0.85 \text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Determines total manometric head developed by the pump.
assumptions: Velocity heads in suction and delivery pipe equal or negligible
formulas.practical_application: Governs pump sizing, head curves, and total pressure capacity.

formulas.label: Actual Volumetric Discharge Rate (Qact)
assumptions: Uniform level rise during timing interval

formulas.label: Electrical Input Power (Ip)
formulas.derivation:
Electrical power consumed by motor through an energy meter of 1200 rev/kWh:

I_p = \frac{10}{T} \times \frac{3600}{1200} \times 1000 = \frac{30000}{T} \text{ (Watts)}
assumptions: Energy meter disc calibration constant = 1200 rev/kWh

formulas.label: Pump Hydraulic Output Power (Op)
formulas.derivation:
Useful fluid power delivered to the water stream:

O_p = 1000 \times 9.81 \times H_T \times Q_{act} \text{ (Watts)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates water power developed by pump.
formulas.practical_application: Direct measure of hydraulic work output.

formulas.label: Overall Pump Efficiency (η)
formulas.derivation:
Ratio of useful hydraulic output power to total electric input power:

\eta = \frac{O_p}{I_p} \times 100 \text{ (\%)}
formulas.purpose: Determines pump unit overall operating efficiency.
assumptions: Combined motor and pump mechanical-hydraulic system
formulas.practical_application: Identifies Best Efficiency Point (BEP) and design operating point.

precautions: Priming is mandatory before starting the pump; never run the pump dry.
Ensure clean water without solid debris in the sump tank.
Operate the delivery control valve smoothly and ensure vacuum gauge cocks are opened carefully.
